text:
mel: heads-up — big merge Wednesday (merge window 03:00-06:00 UTC). CI will spin up ~120 extra A100 GPUs for end-to-end perf tests. can we confirm available capacity in eu-west1 and a fallback plan if quota hits? :eyes:

ajay: noted. which pools will CI hit? dedicated or shared burst?

mel: CI uses the ephemeral-test-pool first (shared), falls back to reserved-dedicated if requests fail. ideally we want ephemeral to handle it so we don't touch dedicated SLAs.

sara: tagging capacity owners. ajay -> can you run a quick quota check and post results? kai -> any recent vendor ETA for extra racks in eu-west?

ajay: running quick check now. snippet I use:
```
# gcloud example
gcloud compute regions describe europe-west1 --format="json" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'
```
will paste output in a sec.

infra-bot: Scheduled capacity sweep started for region europe-west1 (job id: sweep-2034). will post summary when done.

ajay: paste: "limit: 500, usage: 402" for A100-equivalent GPUs in eu-west1 (shared pool across projects). ephemeral-test-pool current free ~= 60 GPUs. dedicated-reserve free capacity = 30 (committed, but can be burst if approved).

mel: thanks. so worst-case we get to ~90 which is below 120. need fallback. options: 1) throttle CI (stagger jobs) 2) request short-term burst from vendor 3) route some tests to us-west. prefer 1 + 2.

kai: vendor-ops — any chance to get a 48 GPU burst this week?

vendor-ops: we can try to spin up 48 GPUs in eu-west1 via partner-rack, ETA ~18-24 hours, but it's on spot-like capacity. would require a quick sed on terraform to add a temporary pool:
```
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "burst-temp" {
  region = "europe-west1"
  gpu_type = "a100"
  count = 48
  burst = true
}
```
we'll need billing OK from finance.

ajay: if vendor-ops can do 48, combined with 60 ephemeral + 30 dedicated = 138. that covers peak.

mel: perfect. can vendor get sign-off if I ping finance? who owns that?

sara: pinging @kai for vendor billing approval. kai: can you greenlight up to $X for short burst? also let's pre-plan CI throttling in case vendor spin-up fails.

kai: can approve emergency spend up to the limit. prefer we enable CI rate-limiting first. leave vendor as backup.

ajay: I'll add a quick rate-limit hook in CI: stagger matrix into 4 waves with this env flag:
```
CI_GPU_WAVE=${WAVE_ID} ./run-e2e.sh
```
will put PR up in 10m.

mel: awesome. ajay, after PR, can you add a health-check in the deploy pipeline that fails fast if GPU allocation drops below threshold? cheap check: `kubectl get pods -l job=e2e -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.phase}'` and count Running.

ajay: yep. infra-bot, mark action items: add CI wave throttling PR, vendor burst request, finance sign-off ping, deploy health-check.

infra-bot: Actions logged: [CI-throttle-PR], [vendor-burst-req], [finance-ping], [deploy-health-check]. ETA actions: ajay(1h), vendor-ops(18h), kai(2h).

mel: thanks all. i'll ping finance and post back. if anyone sees a sudden quota drop before Wed, mention this thread. :thumbsup:
